rules.title: let without initializer
rules.statement: `let v: T;` (no initializer) introduces a binding of declared type T whose storage is uninitialized; the type annotation is mandatory (cannot infer) and a later assignment initializes it. Reading before assignment is forbidden (enforced by earlier definite-assignment analysis).

rules.title: Re-declaration resets init/drop state
rules.statement: A fresh `let` of a name shadowing an earlier same-named binding (e.g. in sequential blocks or per loop iteration) resets that name's definite-assignment and drop-flag state; if the declaration is in a loop body the drop-flag is re-initialized to 0 on each iteration.

rules.title: Conditional init tracked by runtime drop flag
rules.statement: For a declare-without-init binding: if every later assignment statically dominates the binding's uses, initialization is tracked statically and drops are placed unconditionally; if assignment is conditional (e.g. assigned only inside an `if`/loop), a runtime drop flag (initialized 0) governs both drop-before-replace and scope-exit drop.

rules.title: let binding from a place is an independent copy
rules.statement: Binding `let b = a` where the RHS denotes an existing place of aggregate type (struct, enum value-repr, array, slice/str, fat pointer) produces an independent value: the source's full type footprint (sizeof T bytes) is copied into a fresh storage slot, so later mutation of the source does not alias the binding. Move-vs-copy soundness (no double-free) is enforced separately by move analysis.

rules.title: Array let-rebind copies whole array
rules.statement: `let b: [T; N] = a;` where `a` is an existing array place copies all N*sizeof(T) bytes of the source array into the binding's slot (not just a pointer), yielding an independent array binding.

rules.title: Scalar let coerces RHS to annotated type
rules.statement: For a scalar-typed binding `let v: T = e`, the RHS value is coerced to the declared integer/float type T (integer widening/narrowing and float conversion) before storage.

rules.title: Box<Concrete> unsizes to Box<dyn Trait>
rules.statement: Binding a `Box<Concrete>` value to a `Box<dyn Trait>` (or `&Concrete`/`&dyn`/`*dyn`) target coerces the thin pointer to a fat {data, vtable} pair whose vtable is selected for the concrete type's impl of Trait. An owning `Box<dyn Trait>` is droppable: its drop runs drop_in_place on the data and frees it; a `&dyn`/`&mut dyn` borrow yields a non-owning fat pair; only raw `*const/*mut dyn` retains a separately-allocated 8-byte heap handle.

rules.title: Fat-pointer source needs no rebuild
rules.statement: When coercing to `dyn Trait`, if the RHS value is already a fat pointer (its type is `dyn Trait`, or `&/&mut/*` to `dyn Trait`, with Box<dyn> collapsing to the trait object), the existing {data, vtable} handle is used directly rather than rebuilt from the concrete type.

rules.title: AnyVal-typed let binds an i32
rules.statement: A binding declared with type `AnyVal` coerces its RHS to a 32-bit integer and stores it as a scalar binding.
rules.uncertainty: AnyVal is a compiler-internal/metaprogramming type; the i32 coercion may be an implementation default rather than a stable language guarantee.
rules.divergence: No Rust equivalent (AnyVal is a Logos addition).

rules.title: Reassignment drops the old value (static)
rules.statement: An assignment `x = e` to a binding holding a live droppable value first evaluates e, then runs the full destructor (user Drop impl + owned children) of the OLD value, then stores the new value. Evaluating the RHS before the old-value drop makes `x = f(x)` read the old x safely.

rules.title: First assignment to uninitialized binding does not drop
rules.statement: For a binding whose init state is statically tracked, the first (dominating) assignment overwrites uninitialized storage and performs NO drop of the prior contents; subsequent assignments drop the live value unconditionally.

rules.title: Conditional drop-before-replace via flag
rules.statement: When a binding's initialization is not statically known, assignment drops the old value only if the runtime drop flag is set (value live), then marks the slot live; this makes `x = b` after a conditional `if c { x = a; }` drop `a` iff the conditional ran.

rules.title: Whole-struct reassignment copies payload
rules.statement: Reassigning a struct/zoned-struct binding from another struct place copies the full sizeof(T) byte payload into the destination slot (not a pointer store), keeping the binding's storage independent.

rules.title: Fat-pointer reassignment copies 16 bytes
rules.statement: Reassigning a slice, closure, or trait-object binding copies the full 16-byte {data, len|vtable} pair, so neither half (data nor len/vtable) is left stale.

rules.title: Whole-array reassignment copies payload
rules.statement: Reassigning an array binding from another array place copies the full sizeof([T;N]) byte payload into the destination, not just a pointer.

rules.title: Enum reassignment copies inline value-repr
rules.statement: Reassigning a tagged-enum binding copies the new value's inline {disc, payload} footprint into the slot; a bare discriminant value (e.g. `o = None` with no inferred type args) writes only the discriminant word.

rules.title: Storage representation by type kind
rules.statement: A binding's storage representation is fixed by type kind: scalars/fn-pointers/fn-items hold the value inline; structs, zoned-structs, arrays, and value-repr enums hold inline storage addressed by a pointer; tuples, closures, and slices/str are pointer-to-aggregate ({ptr,len} for slices); FnItem (per-instantiation ZST) lowers identically to a function pointer.
